授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（日本語）:
「Comparative Contract Law」（春学期）は、国際取引における契約の重要性と、その機能が異なる法制度でどのように運用されるかを学ぶ。近年の世界的な現象（COVID-19パンデミック、スエズ運河の封鎖、高インフレ、価格変動など）は、契約法に関する重要な課題を浮き彫りにし、個人や企業がリスクを管理・軽減する必要性を強調する。本講義では、主要な法体系における契約法の異なるアプローチを比較し、長所と短所を検討する。主なテーマとして、契約締結前の責任、契約の成立、錯誤・詐欺・強迫、契約履行における予期せぬ事態、救済手段などを扱う。受講者は、英米法やフランス・ドイツ民法などの影響を受けた法制度を比較し、契約法の基礎知識を深めることができる。特に、英仏独の契約法を中心に、アメリカや日本の特徴にも言及しながら、理論と実務の両面から契約法を探求する。
「Criminal and Civil Procedure Law」（夏学期）では、日本の裁判制度、日本の民事訴訟手続および刑事訴訟手続について概説する。学部生（GV学生）とLL.M.学生がともに参加し、講義とディスカッションを通じて、日本の司法制度の構造と機能について基礎的な理解を深めることを目的とする。本講義では、民事・刑事手続の主要な要素を取り上げ、日本における事件の進行および裁判手続の流れを学ぶ。また、比較法的視点を養うため、タイの判事であるKamonchanokさんがタイの民事・刑事訴訟手続について概説し、両国の法制度の類似点と相違点を批判的に考察する機会を提供する。講義の最後には裁判所見学を実施し、日本の司法制度を実際に観察する機会を設ける。この実践的な要素を通じて、理論的な知識を補完し、司法手続に関する実務的視点を得ることを目指す。
授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（英語）:
"Comparative Contract Law"
At the international level, contracts remain the most important legal instruments for international transactions, and understanding their functioning within various legal systems is crucial in today’s globalized world. Several recent global phenomena—such as the COVID-19 pandemic, the Suez Canal blockage, high inflation, and price fluctuations—have highlighted a number of key issues in contract law. As a result, individuals and businesses have been compelled to find ways to prevent or at least mitigate the diverse forms of risk to which they are exposed on a daily basis.
As common patterns emerge across dominant legal traditions, it is vital to examine the different solutions adopted by major jurisdictions, particularly their advantages and disadvantages. This Course will therefore explore several key contemporary issues in contract law, such as precontractual liability, contract formation, mistake, deceit, duress, supervening events, and remedies. It is designed to help participants acquire a fundamental understanding of comparative contract law by offering diverse perspectives on these major issues across selected jurisdictions. The Course will demonstrate that, although individual legal systems may adopt
different solutions, they often achieve comparable results.
Given that many national legal regimes have been influenced by English common law, as well as the French and German Civil Codes, the Course will reference specific legal institutions from those jurisdictions. It will thus combine theoretical aspects with practical applications of individual issues, focusing primarily on English, French, and German contract law, with additional references to specific features of US and Japanese law.
This Course will be conducted in a seminar format, with an emphasis on in-class discussions of current trends and controversies in contract law from a comparative perspective. Particular focus will be placed on the common law, French, and German legal traditions, including their respective case law.
"Criminal and Civil Procedure Law"
This course provides an overview of the Japanese court system, civil and criminal proceedings in Japan. Both Japanese undergraduate (GV students) and LL.M. students will participate in this course, which aims to provide a basic understanding of the structure and function of the Japanese judicial system through lectures and discussion. This course will cover the major elements of civil and criminal procedure and will cover the progression of cases and the flow of court proceedings in Japan.
In addition, to develop a comparative legal perspective, a guest speaker will give an overview of civil and criminal proceedings, providing an opportunity to critically examine the similarities and differences between different legal systems.
The lecture will conclude with a court visit, providing an opportunity to observe the Japanese judicial system in action. Through this practical component, the course aims to complement theoretical knowledge and provide a practical perspective on judicial procedures.
